cards.back: database - 有组织的数据集合
cards.example: A relational **database** stores data in tables with predefined schemas.

cards.back: relational database - 基于关系模型的数据库
cards.example: PostgreSQL and MySQL are popular **relational databases**.

cards.back: NoSQL - 灵活模式的数据库
cards.example: MongoDB and Cassandra are **NoSQL** databases with flexible schemas.

cards.back: NewSQL - 兼具NoSQL扩展性和SQL ACID特性
cards.example: CockroachDB and TiDB are **NewSQL** databases combining scalability and ACID.

cards.back: document database - 存储JSON-like文档的数据库
cards.example: MongoDB is a **document database** storing JSON-like documents.

cards.back: key-value store - 简单的键值对数据库
cards.example: Redis is an in-memory **key-value store**.

cards.back: wide-column store - 按列族存储的数据库
cards.example: Cassandra and HBase are **wide-column stores**.

cards.back: graph database - 以节点和关系存储数据
cards.example: Neo4j is a **graph database** optimized for relationship queries.

cards.back: time-series database - 优化时间序列数据存储
cards.example: InfluxDB and TimescaleDB are **time-series databases**.

cards.back: search engine database - 优化全文搜索
cards.example: Elasticsearch is a **search engine database** for full-text search.

cards.back: atomicity - 事务要么全部完成要么全部不完成
cards.example: **Atomicity** ensures all operations in a transaction complete or none do.

cards.back: consistency - 事务前后数据库处于有效状态
cards.example: **Consistency** ensures a transaction brings the database from one valid state to another.

cards.back: isolation - 并发事务互不干扰
cards.example: **Isolation** prevents concurrent transactions from interfering with each other.

cards.back: durability - 已提交事务的结果不会丢失
cards.example: **Durability** guarantees committed transactions survive system failures.

cards.back: transaction - 原子性的数据库操作序列
cards.example: A **transaction** is a sequence of operations treated as a single unit of work.

cards.back: commit - 永久保存事务的变更
cards.example: **Commit** makes transaction changes permanent in the database.

cards.back: rollback - 撤销事务的所有变更
cards.example: **Rollback** undoes all changes made by a transaction.

cards.back: savepoint - 事务中的中间回滚点
cards.example: A **savepoint** allows partial rollback within a transaction.

cards.back: isolation level - 事务隔离的强度等级
cards.example: **Isolation levels** balance consistency and concurrency performance.

cards.back: read uncommitted - 最低隔离级别
cards.example: **Read uncommitted** allows reading uncommitted changes (dirty reads).

cards.back: read committed - 防止脏读的隔离级别
cards.example: **Read committed** prevents dirty reads by only reading committed data.

cards.back: repeatable read - 同一事务内多次读取一致的隔离级别
cards.example: **Repeatable read** ensures consistent reads within the same transaction.

cards.back: serializable - 最高隔离级别
cards.example: **Serializable** is the highest isolation level, executing transactions sequentially.

cards.back: snapshot isolation - 基于MVCC的隔离级别
cards.example: **Snapshot isolation** uses MVCC for consistent reads without locking.

cards.back: MVCC - 非阻塞读写的技术
cards.example: **MVCC** maintains multiple versions of data for non-blocking reads.

cards.back: phantom read - 同一查询返回不同行集的现象
cards.example: A **phantom read** occurs when the same query returns different rows.

cards.back: non-repeatable read - 同一事务内两次读取结果不同
cards.example: A **non-repeatable read** gets different values for the same row.

cards.back: dirty read - 读取到未提交的数据
cards.example: A **dirty read** reads data that has not been committed yet.

cards.back: lost update - 两个事务同时更新导致一个丢失
cards.example: A **lost update** occurs when two transactions update the same data simultaneously.

cards.back: write skew - 事务基于过期数据做决策
cards.example: **Write skew** occurs when transactions make decisions on stale data.

cards.back: optimistic locking - 提交时检查冲突的并发控制
cards.example: **Optimistic locking** checks for conflicts at commit time using versions.

cards.back: pessimistic locking - 操作前获取锁的并发控制
cards.example: **Pessimistic locking** acquires locks before accessing data.

cards.back: two-phase locking - 加锁和解锁两阶段的协议
cards.example: **Two-phase locking** has a growing phase (acquiring locks) and shrinking phase (releasing).

cards.back: deadlock - 多个事务互相等待对方释放锁
cards.example: A **deadlock** occurs when transactions wait for each other indefinitely.

cards.back: deadlock detection - 自动发现并解决死锁
cards.example: **Deadlock detection** identifies and resolves circular wait situations.

cards.back: wait-die - older事务等待的非抢占式死锁预防
cards.example: **Wait-die**: older transactions wait; younger ones abort and restart.

cards.back: wound-wait - older事务抢占的非抢占式死锁预防
cards.example: **Wound-wait**: older transactions preempt; younger ones wait.

cards.back: index - 加速数据库查询的数据结构
cards.example: A database **index** speeds up queries by avoiding full table scans.

cards.back: primary key - 唯一标识表中每行记录的列
cards.example: The **primary key** uniquely identifies each row in a table.

cards.back: foreign key - 建立表与表之间关系的列
cards.example: A **foreign key** references the primary key of another table.

cards.back: composite key - 由多个列组成的主键
cards.example: A **composite key** consists of multiple columns as the primary key.

cards.back: candidate key - 可成为主键的列或列组合
cards.example: A **candidate key** can uniquely identify rows and potentially be the primary key.

cards.back: superkey - 能唯一标识行的属性集
cards.example: A **superkey** is a set of attributes that can uniquely identify a row.

cards.back: unique constraint - 确保列值不重复的规则
cards.example: A **unique constraint** ensures all values in a column are distinct.

cards.back: check constraint - 确保数据满足条件的规则
cards.example: A **check constraint** validates that data meets specified conditions.

cards.back: not null constraint - 确保列值不为空的规则
cards.example: A **not null constraint** prevents null values in a column.

cards.back: default constraint - 自动填充默认值的规则
cards.example: A **default constraint** provides a default value when none is specified.

cards.back: referential integrity - 外键关系的有效性
cards.example: **Referential integrity** ensures foreign key relationships remain valid.

cards.back: cascade delete - 删除父记录时自动删除子记录
cards.example: **Cascade delete** automatically deletes child records when parent is deleted.

cards.back: cascade update - 更新父记录时自动更新子记录
cards.example: **Cascade update** propagates primary key changes to foreign keys.

cards.back: set null - 删除父记录时将外键设为NULL
cards.example: **Set null** sets the foreign key to NULL when the parent is deleted.

cards.back: inner join - 返回两表匹配行的连接
cards.example: An **inner join** returns rows that have matching values in both tables.

cards.back: left join - 返回左表所有行及右表匹配行
cards.example: A **left join** returns all rows from the left table with matching right rows.

cards.back: right join - 返回右表所有行及左表匹配行
cards.example: A **right join** returns all rows from the right table with matching left rows.

cards.back: full outer join - 返回两表所有行
cards.example: A **full outer join** returns all rows when there's a match in either table.

cards.back: cross join - 返回两表的笛卡尔积
cards.example: A **cross join** returns the Cartesian product of both tables.

cards.back: self join - 表与自身的连接
cards.example: A **self join** joins a table with itself using different aliases.

cards.back: natural join - 基于同名列的隐式连接
cards.example: A **natural join** implicitly joins on columns with the same name.

cards.back: subquery - 嵌套在另一个查询中的查询
cards.example: A **subquery** is a query nested inside another query.

cards.back: correlated subquery - 引用外部查询的子查询
cards.example: A **correlated subquery** references columns from the outer query.

cards.back: CTE - 命名的临时结果集
cards.example: A **CTE** (Common Table Expression) defines a temporary named result set.

cards.back: recursive CTE - 引用自身的公用表表达式
cards.example: A **recursive CTE** references itself to query hierarchical data.

cards.back: window function - 对行集进行计算的函数
cards.example: A **window function** performs calculations across a set of related rows.

cards.back: ROW_NUMBER - 分配唯一连续行号的窗口函数
cards.example: **ROW_NUMBER** assigns a unique sequential number to each row.

cards.back: RANK - 计算排名的窗口函数
cards.example: **RANK** assigns a rank to each row, with gaps for ties.

cards.back: DENSE_RANK - 无间隔排名的窗口函数
cards.example: **DENSE_RANK** assigns ranks without gaps for tied values.

cards.back: LEAD - 访问后续行的窗口函数
cards.example: **LEAD** accesses data from subsequent rows in the result set.

cards.back: LAG - 访问前面行的窗口函数
cards.example: **LAG** accesses data from preceding rows in the result set.

cards.back: PARTITION BY - 窗口函数中定义窗口范围
cards.example: **PARTITION BY** divides the result set into partitions for window functions.

cards.back: OVER - 指定窗口函数的计算范围
cards.example: The **OVER** clause defines the window for window functions.

cards.back: EXPLAIN - 显示查询的执行方式
cards.example: **EXPLAIN** shows how the database will execute a query.

cards.back: query optimization - 改进查询性能的过程
cards.example: **Query optimization** rewrites queries and chooses efficient execution plans.

cards.back: query planner - 决定查询执行方式的数据库组件
cards.example: The **query planner** determines the most efficient way to execute a query.

cards.back: full table scan - 检查表中每一行的查询方式
cards.example: A **full table scan** reads every row, which is slow for large tables.

cards.back: index scan - 使用索引查找数据的查询方式
cards.example: An **index scan** uses an index to find matching rows efficiently.

cards.back: index seek - 直接定位到特定值的索引使用方式
cards.example: An **index seek** directly locates specific values using the index.

cards.back: covering index - 包含查询所需所有列的索引
cards.example: A **covering index** includes all columns needed, avoiding table lookups.

cards.back: composite index - 多列组合索引
cards.example: A **composite index** spans multiple columns for multi-column filtering.

cards.back: partial index - 只包含满足条件行的索引
cards.example: A **partial index** includes only rows that satisfy a condition.

cards.back: functional index - 基于表达式计算的索引
cards.example: A **functional index** is built on the result of an expression or function.

cards.back: Gin index - 通用倒排索引
cards.example: A **Gin index** is a Generalized Inverted Index for complex data types.

cards.back: GiST index - 通用搜索树索引
cards.example: A **GiST index** is a Generalized Search Tree for various data types.

cards.back: SP-GiST index - 空间分区GiST索引
cards.example: **SP-GiST** is a space-partitioned GiST for irregular structures.

cards.back: BRIN index - 块范围索引
cards.example: A **BRIN index** summarizes values in contiguous blocks for large tables.

cards.back: hash index - 基于哈希表的索引
cards.example: A **hash index** is efficient for equality comparisons.

cards.back: B-tree index - 最常见的数据库索引
cards.example: The **B-tree index** is the default and most common database index type.

cards.back: clustered index - 数据按索引顺序物理存储
cards.example: A **clustered index** determines the physical order of data in a table.

cards.back: non-clustered index - 索引与数据分开存储
cards.example: A **non-clustered index** stores index entries separately from data.

cards.back: secondary index - 非主键的索引
cards.example: A **secondary index** is any index that is not the primary key index.

cards.back: unique index - 确保值唯一的索引
cards.example: A **unique index** enforces uniqueness of the indexed columns.

cards.back: bitmap index - 使用位图表示的索引
cards.example: A **bitmap index** uses bit arrays, efficient for low-cardinality columns.

cards.back: inverted index - 从值到行位置的映射
cards.example: An **inverted index** maps values to row locations for fast lookups.

cards.back: full-text index - 优化文本搜索的索引
cards.example: A **full-text index** optimizes searching for words within text columns.

cards.back: spatial index - 优化地理数据查询的索引
cards.example: A **spatial index** optimizes queries on geographic data.

cards.back: database normalization - 减少数据冗余的设计过程
cards.example: **Normalization** organizes data to minimize redundancy and dependency.

cards.back: first normal form - 消除重复组的规范化
cards.example: **1NF** requires atomic values and no repeating groups.

cards.back: second normal form - 消除部分函数依赖
cards.example: **2NF** requires all non-key attributes depend on the entire primary key.

cards.back: third normal form - 消除传递函数依赖
cards.example: **3NF** requires no transitive dependencies on the primary key.

cards.back: BCNF - Boyce-Codd规范化
cards.example: **BCNF** is a stricter version of 3NF eliminating all anomalies.

cards.back: fourth normal form - 消除多值依赖
cards.example: **4NF** eliminates multi-valued dependencies.

cards.back: fifth normal form - 消除连接依赖
cards.example: **5NF** (PJ/NF) eliminates join dependencies.

cards.back: denormalization - 为提高性能引入冗余
cards.example: **Denormalization** adds redundancy to improve read performance.

cards.back: CAP theorem - 一致性、可用性、分区容忍度不可兼得
cards.example: The **CAP theorem** states you can guarantee at most two of Consistency, Availability, Partition tolerance.

cards.back: PACELC theorem - CAP定理的扩展
cards.example: **PACELC** extends CAP with latency vs consistency trade-offs.

cards.back: eventual consistency - 保证最终达到一致
cards.example: **Eventual consistency** guarantees replicas will converge over time.

cards.back: strong consistency - 所有读取看到最新写入
cards.example: **Strong consistency** ensures all reads return the most recent write.

cards.back: causal consistency - 因果相关的操作有序
cards.example: **Causal consistency** preserves ordering of causally related operations.

cards.back: read repair - 读取时修复不一致数据
cards.example: **Read repair** fixes inconsistencies between replicas during reads.

cards.back: hinted handoff - 临时存储不可达节点的数据
cards.example: **Hinted handoff** temporarily stores writes for unavailable nodes.

cards.back: anti-entropy - 副本间同步机制
cards.example: **Anti-entropy** processes synchronize replicas to ensure consistency.

cards.back: Merkle tree - 高效数据一致性验证
cards.example: A **Merkle tree** efficiently verifies data consistency across replicas.

cards.back: gossip protocol - 分布式信息传播协议
cards.example: The **gossip protocol** spreads information epidemically in clusters.

cards.back: vector clock - 分布式事件排序机制
cards.example: **Vector clocks** track causality between events in distributed systems.

cards.back: version vector - 检测并发的机制
cards.example: **Version vectors** detect concurrent updates in distributed databases.

cards.back: last-write-wins - 简单但可能丢失数据的冲突解决
cards.example: **Last-write-wins** resolves conflicts by keeping the most recent write.

cards.back: write-ahead log - 先写日志再写数据的机制
cards.example: **WAL** ensures durability by writing changes to log before applying.

cards.back: checkpoint - 数据库状态的快照
cards.example: A **checkpoint** is a snapshot of the database state for recovery.

cards.back: serializable snapshot isolation - 更强的快照隔离
cards.example: **SSI** detects serialization conflicts in snapshot isolation.

cards.back: predicate locking - 锁定符合某条件的所有行
cards.example: **Predicate locking** locks all rows that satisfy a condition.

cards.back: index-only scan - 只从索引获取数据
cards.example: An **index-only scan** retrieves data without accessing the table.

cards.back: table partitioning - 将大表分成多个小表
cards.example: **Table partitioning** splits large tables into smaller, manageable pieces.

cards.back: range partitioning - 按值范围分区
cards.example: **Range partitioning** divides data based on a range of values.

cards.back: list partitioning - 按离散值列表分区
cards.example: **List partitioning** divides data based on a list of discrete values.

cards.back: hash partitioning - 按哈希值分区
cards.example: **Hash partitioning** distributes data using a hash function.

cards.back: composite partitioning - 多级分区策略
cards.example: **Composite partitioning** uses multiple levels of partitioning.

cards.back: sharding - 将数据水平分割到多个节点
cards.example: **Sharding** distributes data across multiple independent databases.

cards.back: shard key - 决定数据分布的键
cards.example: The **shard key** determines which shard stores a given record.

cards.back: hotspot - 访问高度集中的数据或分片
cards.example: A **hotspot** occurs when a single shard receives disproportionate traffic.

cards.back: resharding - 改变数据分布的过程
cards.example: **Resharding** redistributes data when adding or removing shards.

cards.back: cross-shard query - 涉及多个分片的查询
cards.example: A **cross-shard query** accesses data from multiple shards.

cards.back: co-location - 将相关数据放在同一分片
cards.example: **Co-location** places related data on the same shard for efficient joins.

cards.back: entity group - 需要放在一起的相关数据
cards.example: An **entity group** contains data that must stay together.

cards.back: federated database - 统一访问多个独立数据库
cards.example: A **federated database** provides unified access to multiple autonomous databases.

cards.back: polyglot persistence - 使用多种存储技术
cards.example: **Polyglot persistence** uses different data stores for different data types.

cards.back: ORM - 对象和数据库表之间的映射
cards.example: An **ORM** maps objects to database tables for easier data access.

cards.back: object-relational impedance mismatch - OOP和关系模型的不兼容
cards.example: The **impedance mismatch** describes incompatibilities between OOP and relational models.

cards.back: N+1 query problem - ORM产生的性能问题
cards.example: The **N+1 query problem** occurs when ORM makes N+1 queries instead of 1.

cards.back: connection pool - 复用数据库连接的机制
cards.example: A **connection pool** reuses database connections to reduce overhead.

cards.back: connection string - 包含数据库连接信息的字符串
cards.example: A **connection string** contains information needed to connect to a database.

cards.back: prepared statement - 预编译的SQL语句
cards.example: A **prepared statement** is precompiled for repeated execution with different parameters.

cards.back: database cursor - 逐行处理查询结果的机制
cards.example: A **database cursor** iterates over query results row by row.

cards.back: batch insert - 一次性插入多条记录
cards.example: **Batch insert** improves performance by inserting multiple rows at once.

cards.back: bulk load - 高效导入大量数据
cards.example: **Bulk load** efficiently imports large amounts of data into a database.

cards.back: database trigger - 自动执行的存储过程
cards.example: A **database trigger** automatically executes in response to specific events.

cards.back: stored procedure - 预编译的数据库程序
cards.example: A **stored procedure** is a precompiled program stored in the database.

cards.back: user-defined function - 自定义数据库函数
cards.example: A **UDF** is a custom function that extends database functionality.

cards.back: database view - 虚拟表
cards.example: A **database view** is a virtual table based on the result of a query.

cards.back: materialized view - 预计算结果的存储视图
cards.example: A **materialized view** stores precomputed results for fast access.

cards.back: database migration - 模式变更的管理
cards.example: **Database migration** manages schema changes in a controlled manner.

cards.back: schema migration - 数据库结构的变更
cards.example: **Schema migration** updates the database structure to a new version.

cards.back: data migration - 数据从一个系统转移到另一个
cards.example: **Data migration** transfers data from one storage system to another.

cards.back: schema version - 数据库结构的版本号
cards.example: **Schema version** tracks the current state of the database structure.

cards.back: blue-green database migration - 零停机迁移策略
cards.example: **Blue-green migration** uses two databases for zero-downtime migration.

cards.back: expand-contract pattern - 安全的数据库变更模式
cards.example: The **expand-contract pattern** makes backward-compatible schema changes.

cards.back: cache - 临时存储数据以提高访问速度
cards.example: **Cache** frequently accessed data to reduce database load.

cards.back: cache hit - 请求数据在缓存中找到
cards.example: A **cache hit** serves data from cache without accessing the database.

cards.back: cache miss - 请求数据不在缓存中
cards.example: A **cache miss** requires fetching data from the underlying store.

cards.back: cache eviction - 移除缓存中数据的策略
cards.example: **Cache eviction** removes data when the cache reaches capacity.

cards.back: LRU - 常用缓存淘汰策略
cards.example: **LRU** evicts the least recently accessed item when cache is full.

cards.back: LFU - 基于访问频率的淘汰策略
cards.example: **LFU** evicts the least frequently used item from the cache.

cards.back: FIFO - 按进入顺序淘汰的缓存策略
cards.example: **FIFO** evicts the oldest item in the cache.

cards.back: TTL - 缓存条目的过期时间
cards.example: **TTL** specifies how long a cache entry remains valid.

cards.back: cache invalidation - 标记缓存数据已过期的机制
cards.example: **Cache invalidation** removes stale data from the cache.

cards.back: write-through cache - 同时写入缓存和后端
cards.example: A **write-through cache** writes to both cache and backend synchronously.

cards.back: write-behind cache - 异步写入后端的缓存
cards.example: A **write-behind cache** writes to cache first, then asynchronously to backend.

cards.back: write-around cache - 直接写入后端绕过缓存
cards.example: **Write-around** writes directly to backend, bypassing the cache.

cards.back: cache-aside - 应用管理缓存的模式
cards.example: In **cache-aside**, the application manages cache reads and writes.

cards.back: read-through cache - 缓存自动从后端加载
cards.example: A **read-through cache** fetches data automatically from backend on miss.

cards.back: cache stampede - 大量请求同时穿透缓存
cards.example: A **cache stampede** occurs when many requests hit a cache miss simultaneously.

cards.back: cache warming - 提前加载热点数据
cards.example: **Cache warming** preloads frequently accessed data before it is needed.

cards.back: cold cache - 没有任何数据的空缓存
cards.example: A **cold cache** is empty and must populate data from the backend.

cards.back: warm cache - 部分填充数据的缓存
cards.example: A **warm cache** has some data but may not have all hot data yet.

cards.back: hot cache - 包含大量热点数据的缓存
cards.example: A **hot cache** contains most frequently accessed data for fast responses.

cards.back: local cache - 应用程序进程内的缓存
cards.example: A **local cache** lives within the application process for ultra-fast access.

cards.back: distributed cache - 跨多个节点的缓存
cards.example: A **distributed cache** shares cached data across multiple servers.

cards.back: in-memory cache - 存储在RAM中的缓存
cards.example: An **in-memory cache** stores data in RAM for extremely fast access.

cards.back: persistent cache - 数据不会丢失的缓存
cards.example: A **persistent cache** survives restarts by storing data on disk.

cards.back: cache coherence - 多缓存间数据同步
cards.example: **Cache coherence** ensures data consistency across multiple caches.

cards.back: cache penetration - 查询不存在的数据
cards.example: **Cache penetration** occurs when queries request non-existent data repeatedly.

cards.back: cache breakdown - 热点key过期导致大量请求到数据库
cards.example: **Cache breakdown** happens when a hot key expires and many requests hit the database.

cards.back: cache avalanche - 大量缓存同时过期导致数据库压力
cards.example: A **cache avalanche** occurs when many cached items expire simultaneously.

cards.back: mutual exclusion - 只允许一个请求重建缓存
cards.example: Use **mutual exclusion** so only one request rebuilds the cache.

cards.back: logical expiration - 后台异步更新缓存
cards.example: **Logical expiration** marks data as expired but serves it while refreshing.

cards.back: probation period - 进入主缓存前的观察期
cards.example: A **probation period** tests new items before promoting them to the main cache.

cards.back: W-TinyLFU - Caffeine使用的高效淘汰算法
cards.example: **W-TinyLFU** is the admission policy used by the Caffeine cache.

cards.back: cache replica - 缓存数据的冗余拷贝
cards.example: A **cache replica** provides redundancy and read scalability.

cards.back: cache sharding - 将缓存数据分布到多个节点
cards.example: **Cache sharding** distributes cached data across multiple cache nodes.

cards.back: Redis Cluster - Redis的分布式实现
cards.example: **Redis Cluster** provides automatic partitioning and high availability.

cards.back: Redis Sentinel - Redis的高可用解决方案
cards.example: **Redis Sentinel** monitors, auto-failover, and configures Redis instances.

cards.back: consistent hashing - 缓存节点增减时最小化数据迁移
cards.example: **Consistent hashing** minimizes data movement when cache nodes change.

cards.back: virtual node - 一致性哈希中的虚拟副本
cards.example: **Virtual nodes** improve load balancing in consistent hashing.

cards.example: **HTTP/2** enables multiplexing and header compression for better performance.

cards.example: **HTTP/3** uses QUIC over UDP instead of TCP for reduced latency.

cards.back: TCP - 可靠的面向连接协议

cards.example: **UDP** is a fast, connectionless protocol with no delivery guarantees.

cards.example: **IP** provides addressing and routing for packets across networks.

cards.example: **IPv4** uses 32-bit addresses, limiting the total to about 4.3 billion.

cards.back: IPv6 - 128位地址版本
cards.example: **IPv6** uses 128-bit addresses, providing virtually unlimited addresses.

cards.back: DNS - 域名到IP地址的映射系统
cards.example: **DNS** translates human-readable domain names to IP addresses.

cards.back: URL - 资源的网络地址
cards.example: A **URL** specifies the location of a resource on the internet.

cards.back: URI - 资源的唯一标识
cards.example: A **URI** uniquely identifies a resource, while a URL specifies its location.

cards.back: REST - 基于HTTP的架构风格
cards.example: **REST** is an architectural style using standard HTTP methods for APIs.

cards.back: RESTful API - 遵循REST原则的API
cards.example: A **RESTful API** uses HTTP methods (GET, POST, PUT, DELETE) on resources.

cards.back: CRUD - 四种基本数据操作
cards.example: **CRUD**: Create, Read, Update, Delete - the four basic data operations.

cards.back: GET - 获取资源的HTTP方法
cards.example: **GET** retrieves a representation of a resource from the server.

cards.back: POST - 创建资源的HTTP方法
cards.example: **POST** submits data to the server to create a new resource.

cards.back: PUT - 更新或替换资源的HTTP方法
cards.example: **PUT** updates or replaces an existing resource on the server.

cards.back: PATCH - 部分更新资源的HTTP方法
cards.example: **PATCH** applies partial modifications to a resource.

cards.back: DELETE - 删除资源的HTTP方法
cards.example: **DELETE** removes a resource from the server.

cards.back: HEAD - 获取资源元数据的HTTP方法
cards.example: **HEAD** retrieves metadata about a resource without the body.

cards.back: OPTIONS - 获取服务器支持方法的HTTP方法
cards.example: **OPTIONS** returns the HTTP methods supported for a resource.

cards.back: status code - HTTP响应的数字状态标识
cards.example: HTTP **status codes** indicate the result of a request (200, 404, 500).

cards.back: 1xx informational - 临时响应
cards.example: **1xx** status codes indicate provisional informational responses.

cards.back: 2xx success - 请求成功处理
cards.example: **2xx** codes indicate the request was successfully processed.

cards.back: 3xx redirection - 需要进一步操作
cards.example: **3xx** codes indicate the client must take additional action.

cards.back: 4xx client error - 请求包含错误
cards.example: **4xx** codes indicate an error in the client's request.

cards.back: 5xx server error - 服务器处理失败
cards.example: **5xx** codes indicate the server failed to process a valid request.

cards.back: 301 Moved Permanently - 资源已永久移动
cards.example: **301** means the resource has been permanently moved to a new URL.

cards.back: 302 Found - 资源临时移动
cards.example: **302** means the resource is temporarily at a different URL.

cards.back: 304 Not Modified - 缓存版本仍有效
cards.example: **304** means the cached version of the resource is still valid.

cards.back: 400 Bad Request - 请求格式不正确
cards.example: **400** means the server cannot process the request due to client error.

cards.back: 401 Unauthorized - 需要身份验证
cards.example: **401** means authentication is required to access the resource.

cards.back: 403 Forbidden - 服务器拒绝请求
cards.example: **403** means the server understood the request but refuses to authorize it.

cards.back: 404 Not Found - 资源不存在
cards.example: **404** means the requested resource could not be found on the server.

cards.back: 409 Conflict - 请求与当前状态冲突
cards.example: **409** indicates the request conflicts with the current state of the server.

cards.back: 429 Too Many Requests - 超出限流限制
cards.example: **429** means the user has sent too many requests in a given amount of time.
cards.pronunciation: /fɔːr ˈhʌndrəd ənd twenti naɪn tuː ˈmeni rɪˈkwests/

cards.back: 500 Internal Server Error - 服务器意外错误
cards.example: **500** means the server encountered an unexpected condition.

cards.back: 502 Bad Gateway - 上游服务器无效响应
cards.example: **502** means the gateway received an invalid response from upstream.

cards.back: 503 Service Unavailable - 服务器暂时过载
cards.example: **503** means the server is temporarily unable to handle the request.

cards.back: 504 Gateway Timeout - 上游服务器未及时响应
cards.example: **504** means the gateway did not receive a timely response from upstream.

cards.back: header - HTTP的元数据字段
cards.example: HTTP **headers** carry metadata about the request or response.

cards.back: Content-Type - 实体主体的媒体类型
cards.example: **Content-Type** indicates the media type of the resource.

cards.back: Authorization - 请求的身份验证凭据
cards.example: The **Authorization** header contains credentials for authenticating a request.

cards.back: Bearer token - 授权头部使用的令牌
cards.example: A **Bearer token** is sent in the Authorization header for API authentication.

cards.back: Set-Cookie - 服务器发送Cookie的响应头
cards.example: **Set-Cookie** sends a cookie from the server to the client.

cards.back: Session - 服务器端保存的用户状态
cards.example: A **session** maintains user state on the server across multiple requests.

cards.back: JWT - 紧凑且自包含的身份验证令牌
cards.example: **JWT** is a compact, self-contained way to transmit information between parties.

cards.back: CORS - 控制不同域间资源共享的机制
cards.example: **CORS** allows restricted resources on a web page to be requested from another domain.

cards.back: preflight request - CORS实际请求前的OPTIONS请求
cards.example: A **preflight request** checks if the actual request is safe to send via CORS.

cards.back: Same-Origin Policy - 限制跨域访问的安全机制
cards.example: The **Same-Origin Policy** prevents scripts from accessing data on other origins.

cards.back: handshake - 建立连接时的协商过程
cards.example: The WebSocket **handshake** upgrades an HTTP connection to WebSocket.

cards.back: service definition - gRPC中定义服务的proto文件
cards.example: A **service definition** specifies RPC methods and message types.

cards.back: message type - Protocol Buffers中定义的数据结构
cards.example: **Message types** define structured data schemas in Protocol Buffers.

cards.back: RPC - 调用远程服务像本地函数
cards.example: **RPC** allows a program to execute code on another machine as if it were local.

cards.back: query - GraphQL中请求数据的操作
cards.example: A GraphQL **query** fetches data from the server in a single request.

cards.back: mutation - GraphQL中修改数据的操作
cards.example: A GraphQL **mutation** modifies server-side data (create, update, delete).

cards.back: subscription - GraphQL中实时数据推送的操作
cards.example: A GraphQL **subscription** pushes real-time updates to the client.

cards.back: resolver - GraphQL中处理字段的函数
cards.example: A **resolver** is a function that resolves the value for a GraphQL field.

cards.back: schema - GraphQL中定义类型和关系的结构
cards.example: The GraphQL **schema** defines types, queries, and relationships.

cards.back: type system - GraphQL中强类型的数据结构
cards.example: GraphQL's **type system** ensures queries are valid and type-safe.

cards.back: introspection - GraphQL中查询自身模式的能力
cards.example: **Introspection** allows querying the GraphQL schema itself.

cards.back: callback URL - 接收异步通知的地址
cards.example: A **callback URL** receives asynchronous notifications from services.

cards.back: authentication - 验证用户身份的过程
cards.example: **Authentication** verifies who a user is.

cards.back: SSL/TLS - 加密网络通信的协议
cards.example: **TLS** encrypts network communications for security (successor to SSL).

cards.back: certificate - 验证身份的数字文档
cards.example: A TLS **certificate** verifies the identity of a server or client.

cards.back: public key - 非对称加密中公开的密钥
cards.example: The **public key** can be shared openly for encrypting data or verifying signatures.

cards.back: private key - 非对称加密中保密的密钥
cards.example: The **private key** must be kept secret for decrypting data or creating signatures.

cards.back: certificate authority - 签发数字证书的可信机构
cards.example: A **CA** issues digital certificates to verify identities.

cards.back: self-signed certificate - 自己签发的证书
cards.example: A **self-signed certificate** is issued by the same entity it certifies.

cards.back: mutual TLS - 客户端和服务器互相验证
cards.example: **mTLS** authenticates both client and server using certificates.

cards.back: cipher suite - TLS使用的加密算法组合
cards.example: A **cipher suite** defines the encryption algorithms for a TLS connection.

cards.back: perfect forward secrecy - 即使私钥泄露也保护过去通信
cards.example: **PFS** ensures past sessions remain secure even if private keys are compromised.

cards.back: TCP three-way handshake - TCP连接建立过程
cards.example: The **three-way handshake** (SYN, SYN-ACK, ACK) establishes a TCP connection.

cards.back: SYN - TCP连接请求标志
cards.example: **SYN** initiates a TCP connection request.

cards.back: ACK - TCP确认标志
cards.example: **ACK** acknowledges received data in TCP.

cards.back: sequence number - TCP数据包的顺序标识
cards.example: TCP **sequence numbers** ensure data is reassembled in the correct order.

cards.back: acknowledgment number - TCP期望接收的下一个序号
cards.example: The **ACK number** indicates the next expected sequence number.

cards.back: sliding window - TCP流量控制机制
cards.example: TCP's **sliding window** controls the amount of unacknowledged data.

cards.back: congestion control - 防止网络过载的机制
cards.example: **Congestion control** prevents network overload by adjusting send rates.

cards.back: slow start - TCP逐步增加发送速率
cards.example: TCP **slow start** gradually increases the sending rate to probe capacity.

cards.back: congestion window - 限制未确认数据量的窗口
cards.example: The **congestion window** limits the amount of unacknowledged data.

cards.back: MTU - 网络层最大数据包大小
cards.example: The **MTU** is the maximum size of a network layer packet.

cards.back: MSS - TCP最大数据段大小
cards.example: The **MSS** is the maximum TCP segment size.

cards.back: NAT - 私有IP到公网IP的映射
cards.example: **NAT** maps private IP addresses to a public IP for internet access.

cards.back: port - 标识网络服务的数字
cards.example: A **port** number identifies a specific service on a host.

cards.back: socket - 网络通信的端点
cards.example: A **socket** is an endpoint for sending or receiving data across a network.

cards.back: firewall - 控制网络流量的安全系统
cards.example: A **firewall** monitors and controls incoming and outgoing network traffic.

cards.back: proxy - 客户端和服务器之间的中间服务器
cards.example: A **proxy** acts as an intermediary between client and server.

cards.back: reverse proxy - 代表服务器接收请求
cards.example: A **reverse proxy** sits in front of servers, handling client requests.

cards.back: forward proxy - 代表客户端发送请求
cards.example: A **forward proxy** acts on behalf of clients to access external resources.

cards.back: load balancer - 分发请求到多个服务器
cards.example: A **load balancer** distributes incoming requests across multiple servers.

cards.back: Layer 4 load balancing - 基于传输层的负载均衡
cards.example: **L4 load balancing** routes traffic based on IP and port.

cards.back: Layer 7 load balancing - 基于应用层的负载均衡
cards.example: **L7 load balancing** routes traffic based on HTTP headers and content.

cards.back: health check - 验证后端服务器状态
cards.example: **Health checks** monitor backend server availability.

cards.back: sticky session - 将用户固定到某服务器
cards.example: **Sticky sessions** route a user's requests to the same backend server.

cards.back: round-robin - 按顺序分配请求
cards.example: **Round-robin** assigns requests to servers in sequential order.

cards.back: least connections - 分配给连接最少的服务器
cards.example: **Least connections** routes to the server with the fewest active connections.

cards.back: IP hashing - 基于客户端IP分配服务器
cards.example: **IP hashing** uses the client's IP to determine the backend server.

cards.back: consistent hashing - 减少重新分配的哈希算法
cards.example: **Consistent hashing** minimizes remapping when servers are added or removed.

cards.back: virtual node - 一致性哈希中的虚拟副本
cards.example: **Virtual nodes** improve load distribution in consistent hashing.

cards.back: CDN - 地理分布的缓存服务器网络
cards.example: A **CDN** caches content at edge locations near users.

cards.back: edge server - CDN中靠近用户的服务器
cards.example: An **edge server** caches content close to end users for low latency.

cards.back: origin server - CDN后端的真实服务器
cards.example: The **origin server** is the backend server behind a CDN.

cards.back: cache hit ratio - 缓存命中的请求比例
cards.example: A high **cache hit ratio** means most requests are served from cache.

cards.back: DDoS - 大量请求使服务不可用
cards.example: A **DDoS** attack overwhelms a service with traffic from multiple sources.

cards.back: rate limiting - 控制请求频率
cards.example: **Rate limiting** restricts the number of requests a client can make.

cards.back: throttling - 降低处理速度以保护系统
cards.example: **Throttling** intentionally slows down request processing.

cards.back: circuit breaker - 防止级联故障的模式
cards.example: A **circuit breaker** stops requests to a failing service temporarily.

cards.back: service discovery - 自动查找服务实例的机制
cards.example: **Service discovery** automatically locates available service instances.

cards.back: service registry - 存储服务实例信息的数据库
cards.example: A **service registry** maintains a database of available service instances.

cards.back: health endpoint - 暴露服务状态的API
cards.example: A **health endpoint** exposes the service's health status for monitoring.

cards.back: API gateway - 统一API入口和管理
cards.example: An **API gateway** is a single entry point for all API requests.

cards.back: ingress - 集群外部访问内部服务的路由
cards.example: **Ingress** manages external access to services within a cluster.

cards.back: egress - 集群内部访问外部网络的流量
cards.example: **Egress** controls traffic leaving a cluster to external networks.

cards.back: VPC - 隔离的虚拟网络环境
cards.example: A **VPC** provides an isolated virtual network in a public cloud.

cards.back: subnet - IP网络的逻辑分区
cards.example: A **subnet** divides an IP network into smaller logical segments.

cards.back: CIDR - IP地址分配方法
cards.example: **CIDR** notation (e.g., 10.0.0.0/24) represents IP address ranges.

cards.back: OSI model - 网络通信七层模型
cards.example: The **OSI model** defines seven layers of network communication.

cards.back: application layer - OSI第7层，面向用户的层
cards.example: The **application layer** (Layer 7) includes HTTP, FTP, and DNS.

cards.back: presentation layer - OSI第6层，数据格式化
cards.example: The **presentation layer** (Layer 6) handles data formatting and encryption.

cards.back: session layer - OSI第5层，管理会话
cards.example: The **session layer** (Layer 5) manages sessions between applications.

cards.back: transport layer - OSI第4层，端到端通信
cards.example: The **transport layer** (Layer 4) includes TCP and UDP.

cards.back: network layer - OSI第3层，寻址和路由
cards.example: The **network layer** (Layer 3) handles IP addressing and routing.

cards.back: data link layer - OSI第2层，帧传输
cards.example: The **data link layer** (Layer 2) handles frame transmission between nodes.

cards.back: physical layer - OSI第1层，原始比特传输
cards.example: The **physical layer** (Layer 1) transmits raw bits over physical medium.

cards.back: packet - 网络传输的数据单元
cards.example: A **packet** is a unit of data transmitted over a network.

cards.back: frame - 数据链路层的数据单元
cards.example: A **frame** is a data link layer unit containing a packet plus headers.

cards.back: segment - 传输层的数据单元
cards.example: A **segment** is a transport layer unit (TCP) containing a portion of data.

cards.back: datagram - 无连接传输的数据单元
cards.example: A **datagram** is a self-contained unit for connectionless transmission.

cards.back: MAC address - 网络接口的物理地址
cards.example: A **MAC address** uniquely identifies a network interface.

cards.back: ARP - IP地址到MAC地址的映射
cards.example: **ARP** resolves IP addresses to MAC addresses on a local network.

cards.back: ICMP - 网络诊断协议
cards.example: **ICMP** is used for network diagnostics like ping and traceroute.

cards.back: SSH - 加密远程登录协议

cards.back: DevOps - 开发与运维协作的文化和实践
cards.example: **DevOps** bridges development and operations through automation and collaboration.

cards.back: CI/CD - 自动化构建和部署流水线
cards.example: **CI/CD** automates building, testing, and deployment of applications.

cards.back: continuous integration - 频繁合并代码到主干
cards.example: **Continuous integration** merges developer code into a shared repository frequently.

cards.back: continuous delivery - 自动部署到生产环境
cards.example: **Continuous delivery** automatically deploys code changes to production.

cards.back: continuous deployment - 自动将通过测试的代码发布
cards.example: **Continuous deployment** releases passing changes to production automatically.

cards.back: pipeline - 自动化构建、测试、部署的流程
cards.example: A CI/CD **pipeline** automates building, testing, and deploying applications.

cards.example: A **build pipeline** compiles code, runs tests, and produces artifacts.

cards.back: deployment pipeline - 将应用部署到环境的流水线
cards.example: A **deployment pipeline** promotes artifacts through environments to production.

cards.example: **IaC** manages infrastructure through machine-readable definition files.

cards.back: Azure Resource Manager - Azure的IaC服务
cards.example: **ARM templates** define Azure infrastructure in JSON format.

cards.example: A **container** packages an application with all its dependencies.

cards.back: container image - 容器的只读模板
cards.example: A **container image** is a read-only template used to create containers.

cards.example: An **Ingress Controller** implements the rules defined by Ingress resources.

cards.example: The **HPA** automatically scales the number of Pod replicas.

cards.back: Vertical Pod Autoscaler - 自动调整Pod资源请求
cards.example: The **VPA** automatically adjusts CPU and memory for Pods.

cards.back: Cluster Autoscaler - 自动调整节点数量
cards.example: The **Cluster Autoscaler** adjusts the number of nodes in a cluster.

cards.back: startup probe - 检查容器是否已启动
cards.example: A **startup probe** checks if a container has started successfully.

cards.back: limit range - 限制容器资源使用
cards.example: A **LimitRange** enforces minimum and maximum resource constraints.

cards.example: A **NetworkPolicy** controls traffic flow between Pods.

cards.back: RBAC - Kubernetes权限管理
cards.example: **RBAC** regulates access to resources based on user roles.

cards.back: service account - Pod使用的身份
cards.example: A **service account** provides an identity for a Pod to access the API.

cards.example: A **ClusterRole** defines permissions across the entire cluster.

cards.back: ClusterRoleBinding - 集群范围的角色绑定
cards.example: A **ClusterRoleBinding** grants a ClusterRole across the cluster.

cards.back: Pod Security Standards - 内置的Pod安全级别
cards.example: **Pod Security Standards** define three security levels: privileged, baseline, restricted.

cards.back: OPA - 通用策略引擎
cards.example: **OPA** (Open Policy Agent) provides policy-based control.

cards.back: validating admission - 验证资源的准入控制器
cards.example: A **validating admission** controller validates requests without modifying them.

cards.back: cloud controller manager - 云提供商接口

cards.example: **Pod anti-affinity** spreads Pods across nodes for high availability.

cards.back: 正常路径 - 一切按预期执行的场景

cards.back: 边界情况 - 不常见但需要处理的输入

cards.back: 角落情况 - 极端边界条件
cards.example: A **corner case** is an extreme edge case that's unlikely but possible.

cards.back: code review - 检查代码质量的过程
cards.example: **Code review** improves code quality and shares knowledge among team members.

cards.back: pull request - 请求合并代码变更的提案
cards.example: A **pull request** proposes changes from one branch to another for review.

cards.back: merge request - GitLab中的代码审查请求
cards.example: In GitLab, a **merge request** is the same as a pull request in GitHub.

cards.back: code review checklist - 审查时检查的项目列表
cards.example: A **code review checklist** ensures consistent quality standards during review.

cards.back: peer review - 同事间互相审查代码
cards.example: **Peer review** has colleagues examine each other's code for quality.

cards.back: self-review - 提交前自己审查代码
cards.example: **Self-review** catches obvious issues before requesting peer review.

cards.back: LGTM - Looks Good To Me的缩写
cards.example: **LGTM** means the reviewer approves the changes.

cards.back: SGTM - Sounds Good To Me的缩写
cards.example: **SGTM** indicates agreement with the proposed approach.

cards.back: PTAL - Please Take A Look的缩写
cards.example: **PTAL** requests someone to review the code.

cards.back: WIP - Work In Progress的缩写
cards.example: **WIP** indicates a pull request is not ready for final review.

cards.back: Draft PR - 尚未完成的PR
cards.example: A **Draft PR** is a pull request not yet ready for final review.

cards.back: PR description - 拉取请求的说明文档
cards.example: A good **PR description** explains what, why, and how of the changes.

cards.back: commit message - 描述代码变更的日志
cards.example: A clear **commit message** describes what changed and why.

cards.back: conventional commits - 规范化的提交信息格式
cards.example: **Conventional commits** use a structured format for commit messages.

cards.back: semantic versioning - 版本号传达变更含义
cards.example: **Semantic versioning** uses MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH to communicate change impact.

cards.back: repository - 存储项目代码及版本历史的地方
cards.example: A **repository** stores code files and their version history.

cards.back: clone - 复制远程仓库到本地
cards.example: **Clone** creates a local copy of a remote repository.

cards.back: fork - 创建仓库的独立副本
cards.example: A **fork** creates an independent copy of a repository under your account.

cards.back: branch - 独立的代码开发线
cards.example: A **branch** is an independent line of development.

cards.back: main branch - 项目的默认稳定分支
cards.example: The **main branch** is the default stable branch of a repository.

cards.back: feature branch - 开发新功能的分支
cards.example: A **feature branch** isolates new feature development from the main code.

cards.back: release branch - 准备发布的代码分支
cards.example: A **release branch** prepares code for a new production release.

cards.back: hotfix branch - 紧急修复生产问题的分支
cards.example: A **hotfix branch** quickly fixes critical production issues.

cards.back: develop branch - 集成开发中的代码
cards.example: The **develop branch** integrates ongoing development work.

cards.back: trunk-based development - 频繁合并到主分支
cards.example: **Trunk-based development** frequently integrates code into the main branch.

cards.back: merge - 将一个分支的变更整合到另一个
cards.example: **Merge** combines changes from one branch into another.

cards.back: rebase - 将提交应用到另一个基础提交
cards.example: **Rebase** moves commits to a new base commit for a linear history.

cards.back: cherry-pick - 选择特定提交应用到当前分支
cards.example: **Cherry-pick** applies a specific commit from one branch to another.

cards.back: squash - 将多个提交合并为一个
cards.example: **Squash** combines multiple commits into a single commit.

cards.back: fast-forward merge - 目标分支无新提交时的合并
cards.example: A **fast-forward merge** moves the branch pointer forward without a merge commit.

cards.back: three-way merge - 使用共同祖先的合并
cards.example: A **three-way merge** uses the common ancestor to resolve conflicts.

cards.back: merge conflict - 同一文件被不同方式修改
cards.example: A **merge conflict** occurs when the same file is modified differently in both branches.

cards.back: resolve conflict - 手动合并冲突的代码
cards.example: **Resolve conflict** manually combines conflicting changes in a file.

cards.back: stash - 临时保存未提交的更改
cards.example: **Stash** temporarily shelves changes to work on something else.

cards.back: unstage - 从暂存区移除文件
cards.example: **Unstage** removes files from the staging area.

cards.back: staging area - 准备提交的更改区域
cards.example: The **staging area** holds changes ready to be committed.

cards.back: working directory - 当前操作的文件目录
cards.example: The **working directory** contains the current files being worked on.

cards.back: detached HEAD - HEAD不指向任何分支
cards.example: A **detached HEAD** means HEAD is not pointing to any branch.

cards.back: tag - 标记特定提交的引用
cards.example: A **tag** marks a specific commit as a milestone, like a release version.

cards.back: annotated tag - 包含元数据的完整标签
cards.example: An **annotated tag** is a full Git object with metadata.

cards.back: lightweight tag - 简单的提交引用
cards.example: A **lightweight tag** is a simple pointer to a commit.

cards.back: signed tag - 用GPG签名的标签
cards.example: A **signed tag** is cryptographically signed with GPG.

cards.back: force push - 用本地历史覆盖远程历史
cards.example: **Force push** overwrites remote history with local history.

cards.back: push - 将本地提交上传到远程仓库
cards.example: **Push** uploads local commits to a remote repository.

cards.back: pull - 从远程仓库获取并合并变更
cards.example: **Pull** fetches and merges changes from a remote repository.

cards.back: fetch - 从远程下载变更但不合并
cards.example: **Fetch** downloads changes from remote without merging them.

cards.back: upstream - 你fork或clone的原始仓库
cards.example: The **upstream** repository is the original source you forked from.

cards.back: origin - 默认的远程仓库名称
cards.example: **Origin** is the default name for your remote repository.

cards.back: remote - 网络上的代码仓库副本
cards.example: A **remote** is a version of your repository hosted on the network.

cards.back: submodule - 在一个仓库中包含另一个仓库
cards.example: A **submodule** includes another Git repository within your repository.

cards.back: subtree - 合并外部项目的方式
cards.example: **Subtree** merges an external project into a subdirectory.

cards.back: monorepo - 包含多个项目的单一仓库
cards.example: A **monorepo** contains multiple projects in a single repository.

cards.back: polyrepo - 每个项目独立的仓库
cards.example: A **polyrepo** uses separate repositories for each project.

cards.back: bisect - 用二分法定位引入问题的提交
cards.example: **Bisect** uses binary search to find the commit that introduced a bug.

cards.back: blame - 查看每行代码的最后修改者
cards.example: **Blame** shows who last modified each line of a file.

cards.back: log - 查看提交历史
cards.example: **Log** displays the commit history of a repository.

cards.back: reflog - 记录所有引用更新的日志
cards.example: **Reflog** records all updates to refs in the local repository.

cards.back: hook - Git中自动执行的脚本
cards.example: A **Git hook** is a script that runs automatically on certain Git events.

cards.back: pre-commit hook - 提交前自动运行的脚本
cards.example: A **pre-commit hook** runs checks before a commit is created.

cards.back: commit lint - 验证提交信息格式的工具
cards.example: **Commit lint** validates commit messages against a defined format.

cards.back: code style - 代码格式和编写的规范
cards.example: A consistent **code style** improves readability and maintainability.

cards.back: linting - 自动检查代码风格和潜在问题
cards.example: **Linting** automatically checks code for style violations and potential errors.

cards.back: static analysis - 不运行代码的分析
cards.example: **Static analysis** examines code without executing it to find issues.

cards.back: code formatter - 自动格式化代码的工具
cards.example: A **code formatter** automatically formats code to follow style guidelines.

cards.back: naming convention - 变量和函数命名的规则
cards.example: **Naming conventions** define how to name variables, functions, and files.

cards.back: coding standard - 团队遵循的编码规范
cards.example: A **coding standard** defines the rules and guidelines for writing code.

cards.back: technical debt - 为了速度而妥协的代码质量
cards.example: **Technical debt** is the implied cost of additional rework caused by choosing a quick solution.

cards.back: refactoring - 改善代码结构而不改变行为
cards.example: **Refactoring** improves code structure without changing its external behavior.

cards.back: boy scout rule - 离开时代码比来时更干净
cards.example: The **boy scout rule**: leave the code cleaner than you found it.

cards.example: **DRY**: Don't Repeat Yourself - avoid duplicating code.

cards.back: KISS principle - 保持简单愚蠢
cards.example: **KISS**: Keep It Simple, Stupid - simplicity should be a key goal.

cards.back: YAGNI - You Ain't Gonna Need It
cards.example: **YAGNI** advises against adding functionality until it's necessary.

cards.back: SOLID principles - 面向对象设计的五个原则
cards.example: **SOLID** principles guide object-oriented design for maintainability.

cards.back: Single Responsibility - 一个类只负责一件事
cards.example: **Single Responsibility Principle**: a class should have only one reason to change.

cards.back: Open/Closed Principle - 对扩展开放，对修改关闭
cards.example: **Open/Closed Principle**: open for extension, closed for modification.

cards.back: Liskov Substitution - 子类可以替换父类
cards.example: **Liskov Substitution**: subclasses should be substitutable for base classes.

cards.back: Interface Segregation - 客户端不应依赖不需要的接口
cards.example: **Interface Segregation**: clients shouldn't depend on interfaces they don't use.

cards.back: Dependency Inversion - 依赖抽象而非具体
cards.example: **Dependency Inversion**: depend on abstractions, not concretions.

cards.back: design pattern - 解决常见问题的可复用方案
cards.example: A **design pattern** is a reusable solution to a common software design problem.

cards.back: code smell - 可能暗示深层次问题的代码特征
cards.example: A **code smell** indicates a potential problem in the code's design.

cards.back: circular dependency - 模块间互相依赖
cards.example: A **circular dependency** occurs when modules depend on each other.

cards.back: tight coupling - 模块间高度依赖
cards.example: **Tight coupling** means modules are highly dependent on each other.

cards.back: loose coupling - 模块间低度依赖
cards.example: **Loose coupling** reduces dependencies between modules for flexibility.

cards.back: cohesion - 模块内部元素的相关程度
cards.example: **Cohesion** measures how closely related elements within a module are.

cards.back: separation of concerns - 将不同功能分开处理
cards.example: **Separation of concerns** divides a program into distinct sections.

cards.back: modularity - 将系统分解为独立模块
cards.example: **Modularity** breaks a system into independent, interchangeable modules.

cards.back: abstraction - 隐藏实现细节暴露必要功能
cards.example: **Abstraction** hides implementation details and exposes only necessary features.

cards.back: encapsulation - 将数据和操作捆绑在一起
cards.example: **Encapsulation** bundles data and methods that operate on that data.

cards.back: interface - 定义行为的契约
cards.example: An **interface** defines a contract that implementing classes must follow.

cards.back: API contract - API提供者和消费者之间的协议
cards.example: An **API contract** defines the expected behavior and data formats of an API.

cards.back: backward compatibility - 新版本兼容旧版本
cards.example: **Backward compatibility** means new versions work with old clients.

cards.back: breaking change - 不兼容的接口修改
cards.example: A **breaking change** modifies an interface incompatibly.

cards.back: deprecation - 标记将被移除的功能
cards.example: **Deprecation** marks a feature as obsolete and scheduled for removal.

cards.back: mob programming - 整个团队一起编程
cards.example: **Mob programming** has the whole team work on the same thing simultaneously.

cards.back: swarming - 多个开发者协作完成一个任务
cards.example: **Swarming** has multiple team members collaborate on a single task.

cards.back: knowledge sharing - 团队成员间分享知识
cards.example: **Knowledge sharing** ensures expertise is distributed across the team.

cards.back: documentation - 描述系统或代码的书面材料
cards.example: Good **documentation** helps team members understand and use the system.

cards.back: README - 项目根目录的说明文档
cards.example: The **README** file introduces and explains a project.

cards.back: API documentation - 描述API接口的文档
cards.example: **API documentation** describes how to use the API endpoints.

cards.back: architecture decision record - 记录重要架构决策
cards.example: An **ADR** documents significant architectural decisions.

cards.back: runbook - 操作步骤的文档
cards.example: A **runbook** documents procedures for common operational tasks.

cards.back: wiki - 团队共享知识的网站
cards.example: A team **wiki** is a collaborative space for sharing knowledge.

cards.back: stand-up meeting - 简短的每日团队同步
cards.example: A **stand-up meeting** is a brief daily team synchronization.

cards.back: sprint planning - 确定冲刺期间的工作
cards.example: **Sprint planning** selects work for the upcoming sprint.

cards.back: retrospective - 团队反思和改进
cards.example: A **retrospective** reflects on what went well and what to improve.

cards.back: sprint review - 展示冲刺成果的会议
cards.example: The **sprint review** demonstrates completed work to stakeholders.

cards.back: backlog - 需要完成的工作列表
cards.example: The **backlog** is a prioritized list of work to be done.

cards.back: product backlog - 产品所有需求的列表
cards.example: The **product backlog** contains all desired work on the product.

cards.back: sprint backlog - 当前冲刺的工作列表
cards.example: The **sprint backlog** contains work selected for the current sprint.

cards.back: user story - 从用户角度描述的需求
cards.example: A **user story** describes a feature from the end user's perspective.

cards.back: epic - 大的用户故事
cards.example: An **epic** is a large user story that can be broken into smaller stories.

cards.back: story point - 估算工作量的相对单位
cards.example: **Story points** estimate the relative effort required for a user story.

cards.back: velocity - 团队每个冲刺完成的故事点
cards.example: **Velocity** measures how many story points a team completes per sprint.

cards.back: burndown chart - 显示工作随时间减少的图表
cards.example: A **burndown chart** shows remaining work versus time.

cards.back: burnup chart - 显示已完成工作的图表
cards.example: A **burnup chart** shows completed work over time.

cards.back: Kanban - 可视化工作流管理方法
cards.example: **Kanban** visualizes work on a board to manage flow.

cards.back: work in progress limit - 限制同时进行的任务数
cards.example: A **WIP limit** restricts the number of tasks in progress.

cards.back: Scrum - 迭代式增量开发框架
cards.example: **Scrum** is an agile framework for managing complex projects.

cards.back: Scrum Master - 确保Scrum流程正确执行
cards.example: The **Scrum Master** facilitates the Scrum process and removes impediments.

cards.back: Product Owner - 确定产品方向和优先级
cards.example: The **Product Owner** defines product vision and prioritizes the backlog.

cards.back: Agile - 迭代式增量开发方法
cards.example: **Agile** emphasizes iterative development and responding to change.

cards.back: iterative development - 通过重复循环开发

cards.back: incremental development - 逐步增加功能
cards.example: **Incremental development** adds functionality in small, manageable increments.

cards.back: minimum viable product - 包含核心功能的产品
cards.example: An **MVP** has just enough features to satisfy early customers.

cards.back: proof of concept - 验证想法可行的原型
cards.example: A **POC** demonstrates that a concept or theory is feasible.

cards.back: spike - 研究技术可行性的时间盒
cards.example: A **spike** is a time-boxed investigation to reduce technical risk.

cards.back: definition of done - 工作被认为完成的标准
cards.example: The **definition of done** defines when work is considered complete.

cards.back: definition of ready - 工作可以被开始的条件
cards.example: The **definition of ready** defines when a story is ready to be started.

cards.back: acceptance criteria - 用户故事必须满足的条件
cards.example: **Acceptance criteria** define the conditions a user story must meet.

cards.back: estimation - 预测完成工作所需时间
cards.example: **Estimation** predicts the time and effort needed to complete work.

cards.back: planning poker - 团队估算工作量的方法
cards.example: **Planning poker** uses cards to estimate effort in a consensus-based way.

cards.back: t-shirt sizing - 用S/M/L估算工作量
cards.example: **T-shirt sizing** estimates effort using sizes like S, M, L, XL.

cards.back: dot voting - 用点标记优先级的决策方法
cards.example: **Dot voting** prioritizes items by placing dots on preferred options.

cards.back: fishbone diagram - 分析根本原因的可视化工具
cards.example: A **fishbone diagram** visualizes potential causes of a problem.

cards.back: five whys - 追问根本原因的方法
cards.example: The **five whys** repeatedly asks 'why' to find the root cause.

cards.back: root cause analysis - 确定问题根本原因
cards.example: **RCA** identifies the underlying cause of a problem.

cards.back: action item - 需要执行的具体任务
cards.example: An **action item** is a specific task assigned to someone.

cards.back: follow-up - 后续跟踪事项
cards.example: **Follow-up** tracks the progress of action items after a meeting.

cards.back: escalation - 将问题上报给更高级别
cards.example: **Escalation** raises an issue to a higher level of authority.

cards.back: blocker - 阻止进展的问题
cards.example: A **blocker** is an issue preventing progress on a task.

cards.back: impediment - Scrum中阻碍进展的因素
cards.example: An **impediment** is anything blocking the team's progress.

cards.back: daily standup - 简短的每日团队同步
cards.example: The **daily standup** is a brief meeting to synchronize the team.

cards.back: sprint - 固定时间长度的迭代
cards.example: A **sprint** is a time-boxed iteration, typically 1-4 weeks long.

cards.back: iteration - 重复的开发周期
cards.example: An **iteration** is a single development cycle in agile.

cards.back: release - 将软件交付给用户
cards.example: A **release** delivers software to users or production.

cards.back: hotfix - 紧急修复生产环境问题
cards.example: A **hotfix** is an urgent fix for a critical production issue.

cards.back: patch - 修复问题的代码变更
cards.example: A **patch** is a small code change to fix a bug or vulnerability.

cards.back: rollback - 恢复到之前的版本
cards.example: **Rollback** reverts to a previous stable version.

cards.back: roll forward - 修复后向前推进
cards.example: **Roll forward** applies a fix and moves to a new version.

cards.back: dark launch - 在生产环境测试但不暴露给用户
cards.example: A **dark launch** tests features in production without user visibility.

cards.back: feature toggle - 运行时控制功能启用
cards.example: A **feature toggle** turns features on/off without deploying code.

cards.back: A/B test - 比较两个版本效果
cards.example: An **A/B test** compares two versions to determine which performs better.

cards.back: canary release - 逐步推出新版本
cards.example: A **canary release** rolls out to a small subset of users first.

cards.back: staged rollout - 逐步扩大发布范围
cards.example: A **staged rollout** gradually increases the user base receiving the update.

cards.back: code freeze - 停止代码变更的时期
cards.example: A **code freeze** halts code changes before a release.

cards.back: release candidate - 可能发布的版本
cards.example: A **release candidate** is a version that could become the final release.

cards.back: sign-off - 正式批准
cards.example: **Sign-off** is formal approval from stakeholders.

cards.back: go/no-go - 发布决策会议
cards.example: A **go/no-go meeting** decides whether to proceed with a release.

cards.back: change management - 控制系统变更的流程
cards.example: **Change management** controls how changes are made to the system.

cards.back: incident response - 处理服务中断的流程
cards.example: **Incident response** is the process of handling service disruptions.

cards.back: postmortem - 事件后的回顾和总结
cards.example: A **postmortem** reviews what happened and how to prevent recurrence.

cards.back: blameless culture - 关注系统性原因而非个人
cards.example: A **blameless culture** focuses on system improvement, not individual blame.

cards.back: on-call - 随时响应生产问题的轮班
cards.example: **On-call** means being available to respond to production issues.

cards.back: pager - 接收告警通知的设备或应用
cards.example: A **pager** notifies on-call engineers of production issues.

cards.back: alert fatigue - 因过多告警导致的麻木
cards.example: **Alert fatigue** occurs when too many alerts cause desensitization.

cards.back: playbook - 处理特定场景的详细计划
cards.example: A **playbook** is a detailed plan for handling specific scenarios.

cards.back: war room - 处理重大问题的集中工作空间
cards.example: A **war room** is a dedicated space for resolving critical issues.

cards.back: severity - 问题的严重程度
cards.example: **Severity** indicates the impact level of an incident.

cards.back: priority - 处理问题的重要性顺序
cards.example: **Priority** determines the order in which issues are addressed.

cards.back: SLA breach - 违反服务等级协议
cards.example: An **SLA breach** occurs when service levels are not met.

cards.back: downtime - 系统不可用的时间
cards.example: **Downtime** is the period when a system is unavailable.

cards.back: uptime - 系统可用的时间比例
cards.example: **Uptime** is the percentage of time a system is operational.

cards.back: MTTR - Mean Time To Repair
cards.example: **MTTR** is the average time to recover from a failure.

cards.back: MTBF - Mean Time Between Failures
cards.example: **MTBF** is the average time between system failures.

cards.back: error budget - 允许的停机时间或错误量
cards.example: An **error budget** quantifies acceptable downtime over a period.

cards.back: toil - 手动重复性的运维工作
cards.example: **Toil** is repetitive manual work that could be automated.

cards.back: automation - 用脚本或工具替代手动工作
cards.example: **Automation** replaces manual work with scripts and tools.

cards.back: self-healing - 系统自动检测和修复问题
cards.example: **Self-healing** systems automatically detect and fix problems.

cards.back: chaos engineering - 故意引入故障测试韧性

cards.example: A **coding interview** evaluates your algorithm and coding skills.

cards.back: behavioral interview - 考察软技能和经验的面试
cards.example: **Behavioral interviews** use past experiences to predict future behavior.

cards.back: whiteboard interview - 在白板上写代码的面试
cards.example: The **whiteboard interview** tests your ability to think and code on the spot.

cards.back: take-home assignment - 面试前完成的编程任务
cards.example: The **take-home assignment** lets you demonstrate skills in a realistic setting.

cards.back: live coding - 面试中实时写代码
cards.example: **Live coding** interviews assess how you think while writing code.

cards.back: mock interview - 练习用的仿真题
cards.example: Schedule a **mock interview** with a friend to practice your answers.

cards.back: STAR method - 回答行为面试问题的框架
cards.example: Use the **STAR method**: Situation, Task, Action, Result for behavioral questions.

cards.back: clarifying question - 确认题目要求的提问
cards.example: Ask **clarifying questions** before jumping into the solution.

cards.back: edge case - 不常见但需要处理的输入
cards.example: Consider **edge cases** like empty input, null values, and maximum limits.

cards.back: time complexity - 算法运行时间随输入增长的量级
cards.example: Always discuss **time complexity** when presenting your algorithm.

cards.back: space complexity - 算法使用内存随输入增长的量级
cards.example: Analyze the **space complexity** of your solution.

cards.back: brute force - 最直接但可能低效的方法
cards.example: Start with the **brute force** approach, then optimize.

cards.back: optimization - 改进算法效率
cards.example: Discuss **optimization** opportunities after presenting a working solution.

cards.back: trade-off - 不同方案之间的取舍
cards.example: Every design involves **trade-offs** between performance and maintainability.

cards.back: bottleneck - 限制系统性能的部分
cards.example: Identify the **bottleneck** in your system design.

cards.back: scalability - 系统处理增长负载的能力
cards.example: Discuss horizontal and vertical **scalability** in system design.

cards.back: single point of failure - 系统中断的单一薄弱环节
cards.example: Eliminate **single points of failure** with redundancy.

cards.back: caching strategy - 提高读取性能的方法
cards.example: Describe your **caching strategy** for frequently accessed data.

cards.back: database sharding - 水平分割数据库
cards.example: Explain **database sharding** for handling large-scale data.

cards.back: CAP theorem - 一致性、可用性、分区容忍度不可兼得
cards.example: The **CAP theorem** states you can guarantee at most two of C, A, and P.

cards.back: load balancing - 将请求分发到多个服务器
cards.example: **Load balancing** distributes traffic across multiple servers.

cards.back: rate limiting - 控制请求频率
cards.example: Implement **rate limiting** to prevent abuse and ensure fair usage.

cards.back: microservices - 小型独立部署的服务
cards.example: **Microservices** decompose applications into independently deployable services.

cards.back: API gateway - 统一API入口和管理
cards.example: An **API gateway** handles authentication, rate limiting, and routing.

cards.back: message queue - 异步通信中间件
cards.example: Use a **message queue** for asynchronous processing between services.

cards.back: event-driven - 基于事件触发的架构
cards.example: An **event-driven** architecture reacts to events rather than direct calls.

cards.back: CQRS - 读写分离架构
cards.example: **CQRS** separates read and write models for independent optimization.

cards.back: event sourcing - 用事件序列代替当前状态
cards.example: **Event sourcing** stores state changes as a sequence of events.

cards.back: Saga pattern - 分布式事务的一种实现
cards.example: The **Saga pattern** manages distributed transactions through compensating actions.

cards.back: idempotency - 多次执行结果相同
cards.example: **Idempotency** ensures repeated requests produce the same result.

cards.back: distributed tracing - 追踪请求在多个服务间的流转
cards.example: **Distributed tracing** follows a request through all microservices.

cards.back: health check - 验证服务是否正常
cards.example: Implement **health checks** for monitoring service status.

cards.back: graceful degradation - 功能降级的服务继续方式
cards.example: **Graceful degradation** reduces functionality rather than failing completely.

cards.back: circuit breaker - 防止级联故障的模式
cards.example: A **circuit breaker** prevents cascade failures in microservices.

cards.back: bulkhead pattern - 隔离故障的设计模式
cards.example: The **bulkhead pattern** isolates failures to prevent system-wide outage.

cards.back: backpressure - 控制数据流速的机制
cards.example: **Backpressure** prevents overwhelming downstream services.

cards.back: dead letter queue - 无法处理消息的特殊队列
cards.example: A **dead letter queue** stores messages that cannot be processed.

cards.back: competing consumers - 多个消费者处理同一队列
cards.example: **Competing consumers** enable parallel processing of a message queue.

cards.back: database index - 加速查询的数据结构
cards.example: Explain how you would use **database indexes** to optimize queries.

cards.back: query optimization - 改进查询性能
cards.example: Discuss **query optimization** techniques for slow database queries.

cards.back: connection pool - 复用数据库连接
cards.example: Use a **connection pool** to efficiently manage database connections.

cards.back: ORM - 简化数据库操作
cards.example: Discuss the pros and cons of using an **ORM** versus raw SQL.

cards.back: N+1 problem - ORM产生的性能问题
cards.example: The **N+1 problem** occurs when ORM makes excessive database queries.

cards.back: object storage - 存储非结构化数据
cards.example: Use **object storage** like S3 for storing files and media.

cards.back: CDN - 地理分布的缓存服务器
cards.example: A **CDN** caches content at edge locations for low latency.

cards.back: DNS - 域名到IP的映射
cards.example: **DNS** translates domain names to IP addresses.

cards.back: reverse proxy - 代表服务器接收请求
cards.example: A **reverse proxy** sits in front of application servers.

cards.back: service mesh - 管理服务间通信
cards.example: A **service mesh** handles service-to-service communication.

cards.back: sidecar pattern - 与主应用共存的辅助服务
cards.example: The **sidecar pattern** deploys helper services alongside the main application.

cards.back: blue-green deployment - 两个环境切换的部署策略
cards.example: **Blue-green deployment** enables zero-downtime releases.

cards.back: canary deployment - 逐步推出新版本
cards.example: **Canary deployment** releases to a small subset first.

cards.back: feature flag - 运行时控制功能启用
cards.example: Use **feature flags** to control feature rollout without deployment.

cards.back: observability - 通过输出来理解系统状态
cards.example: **Observability** uses metrics, logs, and traces to understand systems.

cards.back: SLA - 服务提供方和用户的协议
cards.example: An **SLA** defines the expected availability and performance.

cards.back: data consistency - 多副本间数据的一致性
cards.example: Discuss strategies for maintaining **data consistency** across services.

cards.back: eventual consistency - 保证最终达到一致
cards.example: **Eventual consistency** is acceptable for many distributed systems.

cards.back: strong consistency - 所有读取看到最新写入
cards.example: **Strong consistency** is required for financial transactions.

cards.back: distributed lock - 跨节点的互斥机制
cards.example: A **distributed lock** prevents race conditions across services.

cards.back: leader election - 分布式系统中选择主节点
cards.example: **Leader election** ensures only one node handles coordination.

cards.back: consistent hashing - 减少重新分配的哈希算法
cards.example: **Consistent hashing** minimizes remapping when nodes change.

cards.back: virtual node - 一致性哈希中的虚拟副本
cards.example: **Virtual nodes** improve load distribution in consistent hashing.

cards.back: data pipeline - 数据从源头到目的地的流程
cards.example: Design a **data pipeline** for processing real-time analytics.

cards.back: stream processing - 实时处理数据流
cards.example: **Stream processing** analyzes data in real-time as it arrives.

cards.back: batch processing - 处理大量静态数据
cards.example: **Batch processing** handles large volumes of data periodically.

cards.back: ETL - 数据集成过程
cards.example: **ETL** moves data between systems: Extract, Transform, Load.

cards.back: data warehouse - 结构化分析数据的集中存储
cards.example: A **data warehouse** stores structured data for analysis.

cards.back: data lake - 原始格式存储大量数据
cards.example: A **data lake** stores raw data in its native format.

cards.back: security best practice - 保护系统安全的推荐方法
cards.example: Follow **security best practices** for authentication and authorization.

cards.back: OWASP Top 10 - 最常见的Web应用安全风险
cards.example: The **OWASP Top 10** lists the most critical web application security risks.

cards.back: SQL injection - 通过输入篡改数据库查询
cards.example: Prevent **SQL injection** using parameterized queries.

cards.back: XSS - 在网页中注入恶意脚本
cards.example: **XSS** (Cross-Site Scripting) injects malicious scripts into web pages.

cards.back: CSRF - 伪造用户请求
cards.example: **CSRF** tricks users into performing unintended actions.

cards.back: JWT - 紧凑的身份验证令牌
cards.example: **JWT** is used for stateless authentication between parties.

cards.back: HTTPS - HTTP over TLS
cards.example: Always use **HTTPS** to encrypt data in transit.

cards.back: TLS termination - 解密TLS流量的过程
cards.example: **TLS termination** decrypts traffic at the load balancer.

cards.back: zero trust - 不信任任何网络位置的安全模型
cards.example: **Zero trust** assumes no trust based on network location.

cards.back: code review - 检查代码质量的过程
cards.example: **Code review** catches bugs and shares knowledge across the team.

cards.back: unit testing - 测试单个组件的测试
cards.example: Write **unit tests** for critical business logic.

cards.back: integration testing - 测试多个组件协作
cards.example: **Integration testing** verifies components work together correctly.

cards.back: end-to-end testing - 模拟用户操作的完整流程测试
cards.example: **End-to-end testing** simulates real user scenarios.

cards.back: test-driven development - 先写测试再写实现
cards.example: **TDD** writes tests before implementation code.

cards.back: behavior-driven development - 从用户行为角度定义测试
cards.example: **BDD** defines tests in terms of user behavior.

cards.back: continuous integration - 频繁合并代码到主干
cards.example: **CI** merges code changes frequently with automated testing.

cards.back: continuous deployment - 自动将通过测试的代码发布
cards.example: **CD** automatically deploys passing code to production.

cards.back: Infrastructure as Code - 用代码管理基础设施
cards.example: **IaC** manages infrastructure through machine-readable files.

cards.back: serverless - 无需管理服务器的计算模式
cards.example: **Serverless** lets you run code without managing servers.

cards.back: function as a service - 事件驱动的无服务器计算
cards.example: **FaaS** executes functions in response to events.

cards.back: cloud-native - 为云环境设计的应用
cards.example: **Cloud-native** applications are designed for cloud environments.

cards.back: elasticity - 根据负载自动扩展
cards.example: **Elasticity** automatically scales resources based on demand.

cards.back: auto-scaling - 根据负载自动调整资源
cards.example: **Auto-scaling** adjusts capacity based on real-time demand.

cards.back: high availability - 系统高度可用的架构设计
cards.example: **High availability** eliminates single points of failure.

cards.back: disaster recovery - 重大故障后的系统恢复计划
cards.example: A **disaster recovery** plan ensures business continuity.

cards.back: backup strategy - 数据保护的方案
cards.example: Describe your **backup strategy** for critical data.

cards.back: monitoring - 观察系统和应用状态
cards.example: **Monitoring** collects metrics about system performance.

cards.back: alerting - 异常情况通知机制
cards.example: Set up **alerting** for critical system metrics.

cards.example: **Log aggregation** collects logs from multiple sources.
